title: The Ice Fisher
text: An old woman sits on a stool by a hole in the ice, a line dropped into the black water, a lantern beside her. She has not caught anything in years, she says cheerfully, but today she might. The line is moving. Something down there is very big.

options.label: Sit and fish with her a while. She seems so glad of the company.

outcomes.text: She catches something with too many eyes, and gives it to you, and it is good to eat. Nobody asks what it was.
Something catches her line, and pulls, and it is not her husband.

options.label: The wisest asks what she is fishing for, so far out on the ice.

outcomes.text: Her husband, she says. He fell through in the war. She is sure he will bite one day. Nobody has the heart to tell her otherwise.

options.label: Move on before dark. The ice is no place to be at night.

outcomes.text: She waves without looking up, and calls after you to keep your feet dry. The Leader doesn't, and the cold gets in.
